- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00), model tends to overestimate early in horizon; correct by reducing forecasted peaks and smoothing downward drifts.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.20), model often overreacts with sharp upward spikes; cap forecast growth after initial spike, especially in first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model tends to hold or overestimate continuation; adjust downward in 10–15 day horizon if recent price is above 10% above 30d average.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period drops (especially after 20–25 days) — add a 2–3 day lagged decay factor to forecast tail.
- If sentiment is absent or flat, model often fails to capture volatility — introduce small stochastic noise or volatility buffer in 15–25 day forecast range.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30d moving average, model tends to be biased — apply correction by aligning forecast to 30d MA unless sentiment strongly signals upside.
